title: Wall Street to Issue $21B in Bonds for Record $63B Anthropic AI Chip Facility
summary:
Bank of America, Citigroup and Morgan Stanley are preparing a high-grade bond offering of as much as $21B to fund the senior portion of a $63B debt facility for Anthropic. The funding, which the lenders plan to issue as early as next year, supports a separate financing vehicle that will purchase AI accelerators and networking gear from Broadcom and lease them to the AI developer starting in 2027. The arrangement is the largest ever for AI infrastructure, bringing Anthropic's total debt-backed compute financing to $138B.

To secure the deal, Broadcom provided residual value support for the senior lien of the loan, covering approximately $43.5B if Anthropic defaults. Blackstone provides $9B of the $18B junior tier, which carries a yield exceeding 10%. This rate is significantly higher than the roughly 7% typically paid by other borrowers with similar BB+ credit ratings. While the banks provide the primary capital, the deal is structured so Broadcom assumes the bulk of the hardware risk to facilitate the startup's access to TPUs and other XPUs.

SCOOP: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan was getting impatient.

He needed lenders to commit $40 billon in the largest AI debt deal ever—so Anthropic could afford TPUs—but some were getting cold feet.

In the end, Broadcom’s CEO held 11th-hour talks with bank executives over the weekend to get them to finalize their commitments. Broadcom also agreed to higher interest rates on the loans, sweetening the deal. 

With @ajsaeedy @ mattwirz for @WSJ

selectedTweets.bestBit: blackstone takes $9B of the $18B junior tier, with fees pushing its yield above 10%.
selectedTweets.text:
anthropic offered blackstone a 10% coupon to finance its google chips. for reference - borrowers with similar ratings pay about 7% in public bonds.

broadcom, which helps google build those chips, backs the $42B senior tier. 

blackstone takes $9B of the $18B junior tier, with fees pushing its yield above 10%.

It's the same pattern I wrote about earlier this month: in AI chips, the people who make the chips help pay for the customer to buy them.

meanwhile our gpu rental index across 6 providers is +11% in a month. the chips are getting more expensive to rent too.

i'm watching the other $9B of the junior tier. if it places below 10% by year end, probably the financing scare is easing
